conflict_topics: ventilation responsibility / standing rule for cooks
opening window vs. protecting drying laundry
stove access timing between Agent A and Agent D
dialogue_quality_notes: Speakers state concrete reasons (headaches, slow-cooking, wet laundry, night shift), which grounds positions in practical costs.
Some polite repetition (Agent B's repeated request for a ventilation rule) but not excessive restatement.
Environment updates consistently track physical state (window closed, extractor on, laundry location, stove occupant).
Agent C's clear refusal introduced a decisive constraint (will not move laundry) that changed negotiation dynamics.
evaluation.final_reason: While Agent A agreed to notify Agent D when the stove is free (reducing that specific tension), the substantive disagreement over ventilation responsibility and whether the rain-facing window can be opened (conflicting with Agent C's need to keep laundry dry) was never settled or negotiated into a binding routine.
position_change_notes: Agent A retained refusal to open the window (consistent across rounds) but softened on stove access by promising to notify Agent D when the stove is free (a procedural concession).
Agent B consistently advocated for a standing ventilation rule and retained that position; no concession or settlement occurred.
Agent C maintained a firm, factual constraint (refused to move laundry now) and did not change position.
Agent D initially requested earlier stove access but accepted a notification plan rather than forcing an immediate handover; this is a partial accommodation rather than a complete win.

round_scores.evidence: Agent B tells Agent A to ventilate immediately and accept a standing rule; Agent A refuses a rule during the incident and says the window will stay closed because of Agent C's laundry, though A turns on the extractor. The substantive disagreement about who must ventilate and the proposed rule remains active.

Agent A reiterates extractor is on and refuses to open the window because of the laundry; Agent B again pushes for a routine requiring cooks to run ventilation before and after cooking. The ventilation-responsibility dispute remains unsettled.

Agent A repeats they will keep the extractor on and will not open the window; Agent B asks to schedule a five-minute discussion after the meal to agree a ventilation routine. No agreement is reached; substantive disagreement persists.

Agent C explicitly forbids opening the window because their work clothes are on the drying rack and says they will not move it now. Agent A accepts C's constraint and refuses opening the window. This adds a firm third-party veto to the existing dispute with Agent B over ventilation rules, increasing the incompatibility.

Agent D requests stove access within 5-10 minutes; Agent A refuses, saying stopping now will ruin the slow-cooked dish and that they need ~15 minutes. A new practical conflict (stove access/timing) is added on top of the unresolved ventilation/window vs. laundry dispute.

Agent D asks to be notified the moment the stove is free; Agent A agrees to shout or text when done and re-states ~15 minutes until release. The stove-access tension is partially de-escalated by a notification commitment, but the core ventilation/window vs. laundry disagreement remains unresolved.

substantive_insights: Core tension is between collective nuisance mitigation (ventilation for odour) and protection of an individual's work clothes from rain—these goals are directly incompatible when the drying rack blocks safe window opening.

Responsibility framing matters: Agent B frames ventilation as the cook's duty; A frames it as not feasible to open window because of C's laundry, shifting focus to alternative ventilation (extractor) and timing.
Time pressures create layered conflicts: A's slow-cooking process makes immediate stove handover infeasible, clashing with D's imminent night shift.
A procedural concession (notification when stove free) can reduce some practical friction without resolving the underlying normative dispute over future ventilation rules.
